items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 4:1
items.html: (To the question) It is impossible that both of them use a single Keter face to face, unless the Malchut of the first restriction, hidden in RADLA, is revealed — she being the MAN of the Nukva from the first restriction, fit for a face-to-face coupling with ZA in an equal stature. But beforehand, there is revealed in RADLA only the aspect of the Yesod of the Malchut of the first restriction, which suffices for the Mochin of the male, that is ZA, who needs only male MAN, namely the aspect of the Nukva included in the male, called the aspect of Benjamin included in Joseph. Not so the Nukva, who needs true feminine MAN, which is only the aspect of Malchut by itself. And there is no aspect of Malchut in Atzilut but only from the second restriction, called the Malchut of Ima, from which aspect there is no coupling of Gadlut, but only from the aspect of the inclusion with the crown of Gevura of ZA. There is also, in this Malchut, an aspect of a coupling of Gadlut; but since the GAR of the Nukva are not from herself, but from her inclusion in the crown of Gevura of ZA, she is already discerned as smaller than him, for she needs him for the aspect of the inclusion; therefore she is smaller than him. It is thus found that a coupling of Gadlut face to face in a single Keter is not conceivable unless she has MAN of the first restriction, upon which the Mochin of the GAR emerge. And this will not be in the aspect of the feminine MAN belonging to the Nukva, for it is hidden in RADLA and will not be revealed except in the future, in the secret of the cornerstone, as is known. (Item 5).
